method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, macro/import comparison and reverse paraphrase with the established Marathi sequent-calculus canon plus a bounded official-source check for the classical qualifier; not independent or human review.
scope: The first-order sequent-calculus chapter driver: bilingual chapter title, editorial scope note, proof-system tag, import graph, FOL-conditional imports, and chapter hook.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Both the FOL and PL chapter variants are titled The Sequent Calculus, rendered as क्रमवर्ती कलन, while retaining their distinct fol/pl identifiers and shared seq identifier.
samples.checks: Both title arguments are translated identically; the FOL and PL branch structure and all three identifier arguments remain unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The chapter presents Gentzen's standard LK sequent calculus for classical first-order logic. More examples and exercises would be useful. The prfLK tag includes or excludes material relevant to sequent calculus as a proof system.
samples.checks: Gentzen, LK, classical first-order scope, the editorial request for both examples and exercises, include/exclude polarity, proof-system qualification and literal prfLK tag are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The driver imports rules and proofs, propositional rules, structural rules, derivations, propositional and quantified proving material, proof-theoretic notions, consistency and provability units, soundness, identity and identity soundness. Quantifier, quantified-proof, quantified-provability, identity and identity-soundness imports are conditional on FOL.
samples.checks: All 14 imported source paths, four FOL conditionals, their empty alternatives, import order, percent guards and OLEndChapterHook are unchanged.

limitations: No independent linguistic review has been performed.
क्रमवर्ती कलन and the Gentzen form have direct authoritative Marathi support.
अभिजात तर्कशास्त्र is supported compositionally by direct technical use of अभिजात for classical theory, but the full logic phrase was not found directly and remains provisional.
